content: It includes details about authors, publication years, titles, journals, and other publication information. 1. McIntyre PB, Gray SV, and Vance JC (1990) conducted a study on the prevalence of unsuspected bacterial infections in children experiencing febrile convulsions, published in the Medical Journal of Australia, volume 152, pages 183–186. 2. McIntyre J and colleagues (2005) compared the safety and efficacy of buccal midazolam versus rectal diazepam for emergency seizure treatment in children. Their findings were published in The Lancet, volume 366, pages 205–210. 3. McKinlay I and Newton R (1989) explored the intention to treat febrile convulsions using rectal diazepam, valproate, or phenobarbitone. This research was documented in Developmental Medicine and Child Neurology, volume 31, pages 617–625. 4. McMullan J, Sasson C, Pancioli A, and Silbergleit R (2010) performed a meta-analysis comparing midazolam and diazepam for treating status epilepticus in children and young adults. The results were published in Academic Emergency Medicine, volume 17, pages 575–582. 5. Milési C and colleagues (2013) conducted a randomized trial comparing 6 cm H2O continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) with conventional oxygen therapy in severe viral bronchiolitis. Their study appeared in Pediatric Pulmonology, volume 48, pages 45–51. 6. Miyahara A et al. (2009) reassessed the use of phenytoin for treating late-stage progressive myoclonus epilepsy complicated by status epilepticus. This research was published in Epilepsy Research, volume 84, pages 201–209. 7. Mosquera C, Rodriguez J, Cabrero A, Fidalgo I, and Fernandez RM (1987) investigated the prevention of febrile seizure recurrence using intermittent rectal diazepam compared to continuous sodium valproate treatment. Their findings were published in Anales Españoles de Pediatría, volume 27, pages 379–381. 8. Murri L, Arrigo A, Bonuccelli U, Rossi G, and Parenti G (1992) evaluated the use of phenobarbital in the prophylaxis of late post-traumatic seizures. This study was published in the Italian Journal of Neurological Sciences, volume 13, pages 755–760. 9. The National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) published guidelines in 2012 (CG137) on the diagnosis and management of epilepsies, and in 2013 (CG160) on the assessment and initial management of fever in children under five years old. 10. Natsume J and colleagues (2007) examined hippocampal volumes and diffusion-weighted imaging findings in children with prolonged febrile seizures. Their study was published in Acta Neurologica Scandinavica, volume 115, pages 25–28. 11. Ngwane E and Bower B (1980) conducted a double-blind trial comparing continuous sodium valproate and phenobarbitone for preventing simple febrile convulsions. The results were published in Archives of Disease in Childhood, volume 55, pages 171–174. 12. Nolan JP et al. (2010) developed the European Resuscitation Council guidelines for resuscitation, which were published in Resuscitation, volume 81, pages 1216–1276. 13. Obi JO, Ejeheri NA, and Alakija W (1994) documented their experience with childhood febrile seizures in Benin City, published in Annals of Tropical Paediatrics, volume 14, pages 211–214. 14. Offringa M and Moyer VA (2001) provided evidence-based management strategies for seizures associated with fever in children, published in the British Medical Journal, volume 323, pages 1111–1114. 15. Offringa M and Newton R (2013) reviewed prophylactic drug management for febrile seizures in children, published in Evidence-Based Child Health, volume 8, pages 1376–1485. 16. Ogutu BR et al. (2003) studied the pharmacokinetics and clinical effects of phenytoin and fosphenytoin in children with severe malaria and status epilepticus, published in the British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, volume 56, pages 112–119. 17. Pavlidou E, Tzitiridou M, and Panteliadis C (2006) conducted a long-term prospective controlled study on the effectiveness of intermittent diazepam prophylaxis in febrile seizures, published in the Journal of Child Neurology, volume 21, pages 1036–1040. 18. Prasad M et al. (2014) reviewed anticonvulsant therapy for status epilepticus, published in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, issue 9, article CD003723. 19. Takanashi J et al. (2006) identified diffusion MRI abnormalities following prolonged febrile seizures with encephalopathy, published in Neurology, volume 66, pages 1304–1309. 20. Yasiry Z and Shorvon SD (2014) conducted a meta-analysis on the relative effectiveness of five antiepileptic drugs for benzodiazepine-resistant convulsive status epilepticus, published in Seizure, volume 23, pages 167–174.
